title: Hand Phaser Type I
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Standard field equipment
summary: The palm-sized sidearm: a gloss-black shell with an antimony face plate around the photon emitter, a cross-hatched electron aspirator pile on top, and the force wheel and indicator dial beside the operational light.
description: The smallest phaser, carried alone or locked into the Type II pistol. Five effective ranges are printed on the sheet, from heat to overload.
interpretation: The shell is lofted from the plan and side silhouettes measured on the sheet, with the force wheel and trigger tab kept out of the body profile (IoU ≥ 0.96 top, side and bottom; the end view, 0.92, is drawn less consistently). The deflector shield is one continuous antimony rail, the force wheel is a ribbed thumbwheel whose rim rises above the top as drawn, and the access-plate seam, adhesion pad and Phillips screw follow the bottom view. The zig-zag aspirator lattice and the dial graduations are simplified.

title: Hand Phaser Type II
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Standard field equipment
summary: The pistol assembly with a Type I locked on top, as the sheet requires. In front are the topaz beam shield and emitter and the knurled photon accelerator. The gloss-black body carries the dilithium crystal cell and a blue-grey aft section with the force setting dial, and the grip is raked back with S/T firing triggers.
description: A long-range pistol built around the Type I. The printed overall width of 49.40 mm equals the Type I’s own width, which confirms the two are dimensioned as one assembly.
components: Firing triggers: S = safety, T = trigger
interpretation: Lofted from the side and plan drawings with the Type I removed, since the sheet draws it only as a phantom (side IoU 0.97, 0.35 mm). The end view isn’t a consistent projection, so the grip’s width is inferred from it and from View B-B. Only the aft section is blue-grey, following the colour key’s leader. The S/T trigger colour isn’t keyed. Overall depth is 16.1 cm against the printed 15.75, because the finished Type I stands slightly taller than the phantom outline.

title: Ray Gun
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Offensive/defensive area weapon
summary: A turned grey body housing tapering to a rounded tail. An antimony collette steps up to the translucent six-step diamond emitter tube, and a raised black trigger panel on top carries the offensive and defensive pads.
description: An area weapon. Its printed effective areas (3 m at 90 m, 8 m at 180 m) describe a widening field rather than a beam.
interpretation: The body and collette are turned from the measured plan silhouette (IoU 0.99, 0.18 mm). The broken-out side view is partial and isn’t scored. The trigger panel’s rise is measured from the bump in the front view.

title: Communicator
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Standard field equipment item
summary: Upper and lower black shells meet at a gold band. The perforated antenna grille is shown flipped open on its hinge, uncovering the LEDs, the transmit/receive and channel switches and the vent.
description: A 200-gram field communicator rated to 12,000 km, powered by an 006P energy unit.
interpretation: The shells and gold band are lofted from the side, end and top drawings (IoU ≥ 0.98 in every view, checked closed). The perforated gold grille swings out past vertical, about 110°, as the sheet’s dash-dot “antenna open” outline shows. Its 297 holes and 27 edge notches follow the hole lattice measured on the plate. LED and switch positions are read from leader lines that end inside the hole pattern, so they’re approximate. The energy unit, speaker and on/off switch are drawn dashed (hidden) and aren’t modelled.

title: Ear Receiver
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: For non-public reception
summary: A finned antimony receiver housing over a black core, with an energy cell and high-gain antenna grid at the base. On top, the earphone and transparent custom-moulded ear-piece swivel stiffly at about 40°.
description: A closed-loop receiver for all prime subspace channels, used where transmissions are private or the surroundings are noisy.
components: High gain antenna grid and heat sink
interpretation: The housing, fins and stem are turned and lofted from the plan and profile drawings. The earphone housing is set at the 39.8° the plan draws, which agrees with the marked 40°. The drawing is about 3% longer than the printed 6.55 cm, and the model follows the drawing. The ear-piece is moulded to each user, so its shape is the plan’s outline. The antimony parts follow the colour key. The profile view can’t show the ear-piece lip the plan draws, so that view fits less closely (IoU 0.93).

title: Universal Translator
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: U.F.P. standard
summary: A long antimony cylinder. At the front are the raked speech-sensor block and the knurled decoding/encoding ring. Along the top run the computer functions display under its transparent cover and the operator’s speaker grille, and the activating switch sits at 45° near the data storage banks.
description: Used to talk with Federation members and with unknown alien language forms in the treaty exploration territory.
interpretation: Turned and lofted from the side, plan and front drawings (IoU ≥ 0.975). The display’s cells are sampled from the drawn pattern, under a clear cover. The operator’s speaker maze is an illustrative labyrinth, not a copy of the drawn one. The side view prints OFF at switch G and the plan prints ON; the model follows the plan, where G is called out.

title: Sciences Tricorder
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Type I
summary: Shown open as the sheets draw it. The display-control head is swung back on its pivot to expose the video display, sensor array, three indicator lights and three knurled selector knobs. Below are the eight record/play discs and the speaker/mic with its arc-and-star grille, behind an open record-compare lid, and the circuitry section stays closed.
description: Senses, measures, analyses, compares and identifies the surrounding environment, with multi-channel recording and a choice of display modes.
components: Disc selector / channel selector / record-play controls
interpretation: The case is built from the measured front and side silhouettes (IoU ≥ 0.975 open and closed). The head swings 125.6° about the pivot printed 18.54 mm below the top, measured along the dash-dot arc on PDF 112, which leaves the faceplate leaning back about 31° as the PDF 126 section draws it. The record-compare lid opens 103.5°, from PDF 113. The drawings place the pivot 4.8 mm off-centre where the print says 3.08 mm, and the model follows the drawings. The strap tab is cut at the drawn break line, 5.4 cm down. Olive and black can’t be told apart in the halftone.

title: Medical Tricorder
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Standard field equipment item — Type I
summary: The medical variant shares the sciences case. Opened, it shows the life-form functions sensor/analyzer in the exposed bay below the R/P lid, a lower compartment lid swung out, LEDs A–C and controls D–F beside the video display, and a speaker/mic with a wavy grille.
description: A 900-gram field diagnostic unit with 24-channel capability. The sheet notes that its internal circuitry is classified.
interpretation: The case is built from the measured silhouettes, and its sections match PDF 126 (IoU ≈ 0.97). The head geometry and pivot are as on the sciences unit. The R/P lid opens 100.3°. The lower lid opens 57°, from two separate checks on PDF 125, though PDF 126 sketches it nearer 30°. The strap tab is cut at the drawn break line, 2.4 cm down. The analyzer’s colour isn’t settled by the halftone.

title: Heartbeat Reader
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: Shaped like a microphone. A spherical guard and ground-plane screen, joined by a clamp band, enclose the omnidirectional sensor. The body carries the BPM readout, two indicators and the activate/audible slide switches, and the base holds the sample and volume selector.
description: Reads the heartbeats of one or many life forms at once. By cancelling known individuals one at a time, it can pick out an alien disguised within a group.
components: Guard and anti-stray audible noise screen
interpretation: The body, screens and base are turned from the measured front elevation (IoU 0.98). The base end view is scored separately. The sensor head is a light antimony sphere under a fine woven grid, as drawn. The sheet doesn’t label the indicator colours, so blue (cancel) and red (go) are inferred from the stipple in the colour key. The drawing is about 0.8% longer than printed, and the model follows the drawing.

title: Spray Applicator
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: A transparent, fluted pressurised vial on an antimony applicator body. The spray trigger is pressed from the side, and an interchangeable nozzle is fitted at the base.
description: Applies external medications, antibiotics and protective dressings to small wounds and contusions.

specs.label: Nozzles (orifice dia.)
specs.value: Extra fine .0025 · fine .025 · medium .20 mm · coarse special order

colourKey.name: Antimony (basic; otherwise matches the vial contents’ colour code)

interpretation: Turned from the measured elevations of the applicator and the vial (IoU ≥ 0.97). The vial is clear because its colour follows its contents. Its forty ribs and the nozzle’s half-round notches follow the drawing. The teat, hidden inside the body when assembled, is grey.

title: Medical Scanner
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: A grey computer housing with ten flutes. Its top dial reads six emission groups against the normal Terran range. Below the collar, the rotating scanner turns inside a 48-mesh screen above the ground-plane screen and life-form scale.
description: Assesses the general medical condition of intelligent life forms by sensing body emanations in alpha, beta, gamma, Kirlian, theta and xi groups.

specs.label: Reading groups
specs.value: A, B, Γ, K, Θ, Ξ

components: (E) Readings dial (increase from bottom to top)
interpretation: Turned from the measured elevation (IoU 0.99). The housing has the ten flutes the dial view’s scallops show, and the dial is turned as the sheet’s “ROT 180° CW” note directs (the note is ambiguous; the silhouette is the same either way). The dark 48-mesh screen is partly see-through, so the rotating scanner’s twisted white vanes show through it as drawn. The life-form scale letters are illegible in the scan.

title: Anabolic Protoplaser
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Portable wound healer
summary: The minor-injury size 0 (left) and the massive-injury size 2 (right). Size 0 has a grey housing on a black removable bottom panel and tapers to a pointed ray emission duct. Size 2 is all grey, with a side activating switch (black off / red on), an effectivity-sensor nub at the front, and a DNA match unit that flares into a blunt cylinder with a recessed duct.
description: Standard field wound healers in two sizes. The larger unit runs up to 500 EmV/AU².
interpretation: Each size is lofted from its own plan and side drawings (IoU ≥ 0.94; size-2 side view 0.99). The size-0 front elevation is drawn 3.56 cm wide against a printed 3.8, and the model follows the plan and the print. Size 2’s side switch is shown, though its front elevation omits it. Drawn heights run 2–3% over the printed figures.

title: Surgical Scalpels
sizeBasis: model envelope in cm (Blender, see model-source/accuracy/envelopes.json)
subtitle: Star Fleet College of Medicine standard
summary: Three laser scalpels in rodinium housings. A ribbed surgeon’s grip carries the intensity scale, trigger and range scale lock under a prime-focus cone, which grows taller and blunter as cutting width increases.
description: Cutting widths of 1, 2 and 3 AU. Intensity falls from 0–80 to 0–70 EmV/AU² as the width increases.
interpretation: The sheet prints no dimensions. Each body is turned from its own elevation, measured at the 0–4 cm bar (IoU ≥ 0.96). The end views are drawn 2–3% smaller than the elevations, so grip radii split the difference. The triggers are the drawn ellipses projected onto the grip.

title: Vulcan Lyrette
subtitle: Orchestral model musical instrument
summary: A harp-like board instrument: a dark Li’pon neck rises to a scroll and carries the fret bar and its eridanite pins, the strings fan down over a mother-of-pearl bridge to an anchor above the tension boss, and a pale Sher Skah voice box carries a nacre control box with four knobs.
description: The sheet calls it an instrument of Vulcan antiquity that combines the tones of harp, lute, sitar and, to some extent, violin. Its tonal pattern is modal diatonic rather than chromatic. Played with the fingers of the right hand, or with a plectrum.

specs.label: Famous makers
specs.value: Sarpk (some 300 survive, about 5 Vulcan centuries old); Sajek of Vulcan; Separ of Trilan

interpretation: The sheet prints no dimensions, so everything is measured at its 0–40 cm bar: the drawn instrument stands about 117 cm, an orchestral size. The side view is a board of constant 4.2 cm thickness, so the measured front outline is extruded and its materials are traced from the key’s stipples (front IoU 0.94, where the densely inked string field beside the neck accounts for most of the mismatch; side IoU 0.91, 1.6 mm mean). Pin, knob, boss and glide heights are read off the side view. The inside of the boss, the back face (plain wood here), the string count and the bridge’s rope binding are interpretations.
printedSize: Not dimensioned · ≈ 117 cm tall as drawn
